candidate_relations.reason: A locally invasive left adrenal mass on azathioprine is not renal cell carcinoma with adrenal metastasis; no renal primary is shown.
An autoimmune flare does not account for a necrotic 7-cm adrenal mass invading pancreas, diaphragm, and spleen.
Infection is not the requested Epstein-Barr virus–associated polymorphic lymphoproliferative disorder.
No hypertensive crisis or catecholamine data support pheochromocytoma as the adrenal lesion.
Autoimmune-associated lymphoma is related iatrogenic lymphoproliferation but asserts lymphoma rather than EBV-associated polymorphic LPD of the adrenal.
Adrenal cortical carcinoma is a different cortical epithelial malignancy, not polymorphic LPD.
Autoimmune-related malignancy is a compatible immunosuppression-associated parent but omits EBV-associated polymorphic LPD involving the adrenal.
The longstanding autoimmune disorder is comorbidity and azathioprine indication, not the adrenal lymphoproliferative diagnosis.
Adrenal metastasis implies a distant primary that is not shown; the reference is primary adrenal LPD.
Metastatic renal cell carcinoma is unsupported without a renal primary.
Adrenal gland neoplasm locates the mass but lacks EBV-associated polymorphic lymphoproliferative specificity.
Renal cell carcinoma is a kidney cancer, not an adrenal polymorphic LPD.
Lymphoma with adrenal involvement is related lymphoid neoplasia but conflicts with polymorphic LPD rather than frank lymphoma, and omits EBV.
Lymphoma is a related but incompatible lymphoproliferative subtype versus EBV-associated polymorphic LPD.
Autoimmune-related adrenalitis is inflammatory, not a necrotic locally invasive lymphoproliferative mass.

case_quality_flags: record lacks EBV testing and tissue diagnosis of the adrenal mass
